# Migration - Split package in a *named* and *unnamed* module

There can be a situation where a split package exists in a named and unnamed
modules. The Java runtime will simply ignore the package found in the *unnamed*
module. Consider the following application.

| JAR File     | JAR Type | Loaded As | Dependencies | Main Method |
| ------------ | -------- | --------- | ------------ | :---------: |
| `app.jar`    | Modular  | Unnamed   | `domain.jar` |   **YES**   |
| `domain.jar` | Modular  | Named     |              |     No      |

The `app.jar` is an unnamed module and contains a split package also found in
the `domain.jar` (on purpose for demonstration purpose).

## Prerequisites

- [Oracle Java 25](https://www.oracle.com/java/technologies/downloads/#java25)

## Run the example

1. Build the application

   ```shell
   ./mvnw clean package
   ```

   (*Optional*) Verify that the JAR file was created and copied to the
   `./target/libs` directory.

   ```shell
   tree --sort=name './target/libs'
   ```

   The application JAR files

   ```
   ./target/libs
   ├── app.jar
   └── domain.jar

   1 directory, 2 files
   ```

2. List all modules

   ```shell
   java --module-path './target/libs' --list-modules
   ```

3. Describe the JAR files

   Describe the `domain.jar`

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/domain.jar'
   ```

   The domain module description

   ```
   demo.domain@1.0.0 jar:file:///./target/libs/domain.jar!/module-info.class
   exports demo.domain
   requires java.base mandated
   ```

   Describe the `app.jar`

   ```shell
   jar --describe-module --file './target/libs/app.jar'
   ```

   The application module description

   ```
   No module descriptor found. Derived automatic module.

   demo.app automatic
   requires java.base mandated
   contains demo.app
   contains demo.domain
   main-class demo.app.Main
   ```

4. Run the application

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/app.jar' \
     --module-path './target/libs/domain.jar' \
     --module demo.app
   ```

   The application fails to launch because the `demo.domain` (`domain.jar`) and
   `demo.app` (`app.jar`) modules share the same package name (`demo.domain`).

   ```
   Error occurred during initialization of boot layer
   java.lang.module.FindException: Module demo.app not found
   ```

   The package `demo.domain` within the `app.jar` is ignored to avoid problems
   related to the split package, as this clashes with a packaged found within a
   *named* module.

   The application runs well when using the class path instead.

   ```shell
   java \
     --class-path './target/libs/*' \
     demo.app.Main
   ```

   The application works and prints the following.

   ```
   "Learn from yesterday, live for today, hope for tomorrow. The important thing is not to stop questioning."
   by Albert Einstein
   ```

   Please note that both JAR files are now loaded as unnamed modules, and are
   therefore subject to issues related to split packages.
